title: Records of Processing Activities + DPIA determination (RODO/GDPR Art.30 / Art.35)
description: Schema for the CyberForge Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) document. RODO/GDPR Art.30(1) requires a controller to maintain a record carrying, per processing activity: controller (and joint-controller / representative / DPO) identity + contact; purposes of processing; categories of data subjects and of personal data; categories of recipients (incl. third countries); third-country transfers + safeguards; envisaged erasure time limits (retention); and a general description of the Art.32 technical & organisational security measures. Art.30(2) covers the processor record (processor identity, each controller acted for, categories of processing carried out on behalf, transfers, Art.32 measures). Polish RODO additionally requires a documented lawful basis (Art.6/Art.9). Art.35 requires a DPIA for high-risk processing; where a processing activity is NOT high-risk the absence of a DPIA must be a documented determination (dpia_not_required_reason), never silence. The validator (validate-ropa.py, task T-22) asserts presence + per-activity Art.30 completeness + the DPIA determination logic. HONEST FRAMING: the validator checks that the RoPA is COMPLETE and INTERNALLY CONSISTENT as a discrete artifact (struktura §12); it does NOT and cannot verify that the recorded controller details, retention periods, or security measures are factually true or that a separate DPIA document is itself adequate — those are EVIDENCE-ONLY facts asserted in the record by the data controller.

meta.description: Document metadata. owner and last_reviewed support the evidence-freshness audit; document_id/version aid traceability.

owner.description: Accountable owner of the RoPA (typically the DPO or, where no DPO is appointed, the data controller).

last_reviewed.description: UTC ISO-8601 date the RoPA was last reviewed. Used for freshness reporting.

dpo.description: Data Protection Officer (Art.37). Optional: if no DPO is required/appointed, omit and record the rationale in dpia_determination.notes or meta.

representative.description: Art.27 representative in the Union, where the controller is not established in the EU. Optional.

dpia_determination.description: The organisation-level Art.35 DPIA determination. This makes the 'is a DPIA required?' decision an EXPLICIT, documented artifact rather than silence (hint / struktura §12). Per-activity DPIA references still live on each activity; this block records the overall posture and its rationale.

status.description: Overall DPIA posture across all recorded activities.

reason.description: Documented rationale for the determination. When status is 'not-required' this MUST explain why no Art.35 high-risk criterion is met (e.g. no large-scale processing of special categories, no systematic monitoring). Silence is not acceptable.

dpia_refs.description: References to any DPIA documents performed (paths, IDs or URLs). Required to be non-empty when status is 'required' or 'completed'.

activities.description: The list of processing activities. RODO Art.30 requires a record PER processing activity. MUST be non-empty: an organisation that operates a CI/CD pipeline processes at minimum developer git-metadata (Art.30 still applies). If you truly process no personal data, that is itself a determination to document in dpia_determination, but the activities array should still record the activities you DO perform.

contact.description: Contact detail — email, postal address, or phone.

controller_identity.description: Art.30(1)(a): name and contact details of the controller (and joint controller where applicable).

activity.description: A single processing activity carrying the full RODO Art.30(1) field set plus the Polish-RODO lawful-basis (Art.6/9) and the Art.35 DPIA marker. role distinguishes a controller record (Art.30(1)) from a processor record (Art.30(2)).

role.description: Whether this record is kept as a controller (Art.30(1)) or processor (Art.30(2)).

controllers_acted_for.description: Art.30(2)(a): for a processor record, each controller on whose behalf the processing is carried out. Recommended (and expected) when role is 'processor'.

purposes.description: Art.30(1)(b): the purposes of the processing. At least one purpose is required.

lawful_basis.description: RODO Art.6 (and Art.9 condition where special categories are processed) lawful basis. Required by Polish RODO practice; an empty/absent lawful basis is a FAIL.

data_subject_categories.description: Art.30(1)(c): categories of data subjects (e.g. employees, developers, contractors).

personal_data_categories.description: Art.30(1)(c): categories of personal data (e.g. name, email, IP address).

special_categories.description: Art.9 special categories of personal data processed, if any. Empty array means none.

recipients.description: Art.30(1)(d): categories of recipients to whom the data are/will be disclosed (incl. recipients in third countries). An empty array is permitted but must be an explicit, conscious empty list (no recipients).

retention.description: Art.30(1)(f): envisaged time limits for erasure of the data ('where possible'). Recorded as a string (e.g. '5 years (DORA Art.12)', 'duration of employment + 6 years'). An empty/absent retention is a FAIL — 'where possible' is satisfiable here, so silence is not acceptable.

security_measures.description: Art.30(1)(g): a general description of the Art.32(1) technical and organisational security measures. At least one measure is required.

high_risk.description: Art.35 marker: true if this activity is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons (large-scale special-category processing, systematic monitoring, etc.). Drives the DPIA requirement: high_risk=true REQUIRES a non-empty dpia_ref; high_risk=false REQUIRES a dpia_not_required_reason.

dpia_ref.description: Reference (path/ID/URL) to the Art.35 DPIA for this activity. MUST be non-empty when high_risk is true.

dpia_not_required_reason.description: Documented reason why an Art.35 DPIA is not required for this activity. MUST be present and meaningful when high_risk is false. This closes the 'silence' gap: the absence of a DPIA must be a determination, not an omission.

transfers.description: Art.30(1)(e): transfers of personal data to a third country or international organisation, with identification and safeguards.

occurs.description: True if any personal data is transferred outside the EEA.

destinations.description: Identification of each third country / international organisation. Expected non-empty when occurs is true.

safeguards.description: Art.46/49 safeguards (e.g. SCCs, adequacy decision). Expected non-empty when occurs is true.
